title: Transport: 3DS SO_ERROR is a raw Horizon code; keep waiting while connect is in progress
description: Truck test with the fake connection test: 3DS on V-LINK (192.168.0.151), CONNECT to 192.168.0.10:35000 fails after 3 s with 'errno 26 at connect(): Text file busy'. libctru's getsockopt(SO_ERROR) returns the raw 3DS socket error (26 = EINPROGRESS in the Horizon table), not a newlib errno, so the transport misreports it and gives up as 'refused'. Map 3DS SO_ERROR values to errno, treat in-progress as still connecting until the deadline (re-check with connect(): EISCONN means connected), and report a timeout as 'Adapter did not answer'.
close_reason: tcp_transport_connect: after poll, SO_ERROR on the 3DS is mapped with tp_3ds_soc_errno (Horizon table from libctru soc_common.c; 26 = EINPROGRESS); in-progress re-checks with connect() (0/EISCONN = connected) and keeps waiting in 20 ms steps until the deadline, then TP_ERR_TIMEOUT 'Adapter did not answer'. Host test for the mapping; 80 host tests pass; .3dsx and .cia build with no warnings. Hardware result goes on gauge-boy-7v5.22.

Recommendation: write original short descriptions, cross-checking code coverage and meaning against these lists.

title: OBD reply assembly for all protocols (per ECU, multi-frame, headers on/off)
description: Foundation for every M1 decoder (source/obd/, platform-free, host-tested). Turn an ELM327 reply (cleaned lines) into messages per ECU for every protocol family (brief 1.7.0 section 4). CAN (ELM protocols 6-C): headers off = single-frame lines, or a length line plus '0:'/'1:' ISO-TP lines; headers on = 11-bit '7E8 ...' or 29-bit '18 DA F1 10 ...' with PCI byte (single, first, consecutive frames), grouped by ID. Legacy J1850 / ISO 9141-2 / KWP (1-5): headers off = one frame per line; headers on = 3-byte header (KWP may add a length byte), ID = source address, trailing check byte dropped. Spaces on or off. Output: per ECU an optional ID and a list of messages (CAN: one reassembled message; legacy: one per frame) starting at the response service byte. Bad / partial lines rejected without crashing; tests include real Ridgeline ISO 9141-2 lines (VIN bytes replaced).
close_reason: source/obd/obd_reply.{h,c}: obd_family() and obd_assemble() turn ELM327 reply lines into messages per ECU for every protocol: CAN headers off (single frames, length line + N: ISO-TP lines), CAN headers on (11/29-bit IDs, PCI single/first/consecutive, flow control skipped), legacy headers off (one frame per line) and on (3/4-byte header, ID = source, 9141/KWP sum check verified, J1850 CRC dropped); spaces on or off. Partial, out-of-order and malformed lines are counted and skipped; unfinished messages are dropped, never returned half. 7 host tests (99 total pass) incl. the Ridgeline's real ISO 9141-2 layout; 3DS build clean.

comments.author: ly-man-do
comments.text: Likely cause of the ~400 ms floor (from 3dsDL's docs, GPL, read for study only): on the 3DS every socket call in the process goes through one session with the soc service, which handles one request at a time, so a thread blocked in poll() with a timeout holds up every other thread's socket calls. GaugeBoy's conntest thread loops on poll(..., 100 ms) (CT_POLL_MS), so each of the adapter thread's calls per request (flush read, send, poll, recv) can wait up to ~100 ms: ~4 x 100 ms fits the measured 393-400 ms, and Azahar (no shared session) takes 16 ms. Fix to try: never poll() with a timeout on the 3DS; poll(..., 0) and sleep between checks (1 ms at first, then 5, then 20) in both the transport and the conntest thread, and keep conntest's own waits outside the service. Adapter hardware (Elektroda teardown of a Vgate OBD2 Wi-Fi unit, same 192.168.0.10:35000 bridge): PIC18F25K80 ELM327 board + Hi-Flying HF-LPT230 Wi-Fi module (FCC ID 2ACSV-HF-LPT230), UART 38400 bps, transparent TCP-serial bridge, ~50 mA active, auto sleep after inactivity (1 mA).

title: Choose which Wi-Fi connection slot (1, 2 or 3) GaugeBoy uses
description:
Owner request (2026-11-15): let the user pick the adapter's connection slot so a known network in range (e.g. home Wi-Fi in slot 1 while parked in the driveway) doesn't take over and the user doesn't have to delete it. Today CONNECT asks the 3DS to join any saved slot (ACU_SetAllowApType 0xFF) and skips the join when the 3DS is already on a network, so it can stay on the wrong one.

Design notes:
- Setting: [adapter] wifi_slot = 0 (any) / 1 / 2 / 3 in config.ini; chosen by touch in SETUP (and the Wi-Fi guide, gauge-boy-bxf.1), showing each slot's network name (ACI_LoadNetworkSetting(i) + ACI_GetNetworkWirelessEssidSecuritySsid, as Rosalina does).
- Join only that slot: ACU_SetAllowApType(cfg, 1 << (slot - 1)); bit 0 = slot 1 (Rosalina and emulators; libctru's AC_AP_TYPE_SLOTn names are one bit off).
- If the 3DS is already on a network: compare its network name (ACU_GetSSID) with the chosen slot's; if it differs or can't be read, close and rejoin: AC CloseAsync (command 0x8: ProcessId + event; GetCloseResult 0x9; no libctru wrapper), then ConnectAsync for the chosen slot. Log each step.
- Unknown, test on hardware: whether ACU_GetSSID works for a network the system joined, and whether an app's CloseAsync/ConnectAsync can move the 3DS off a network the HOME menu joined (home Wi-Fi in range is the test case).
- Show the slot and network name in the Network line / header.
close_reason: Done by the SLOT spike (gauge-boy-7v5.29) and the SETUP Wi-Fi slot row: wifi_slot in config.ini, slot names listed, join only the chosen slot, leave another network and rejoin (CloseAsync + ConnectAsync). Owner logs 2026-11-15 16:26 and 16:29 show it moving from the home network to V-LINK in about 3 s on both cars.

title: CAN: several PIDs in one request (up to 6) for LIVE
description: On ISO 15765-4 CAN a Mode 01 request may carry up to 6 PIDs (e.g. 010C0D05110B0F); the reply lists each PID with its bytes. Car Scanner says this makes reads up to 6x faster; the OBD-II standard only allows it on CAN, so not for the Ridgeline or Tracker. Decode the combined reply (obd_reply already reassembles multi-frame CAN), group due PIDs per request, fall back to single requests if the car answers with fewer. Test on the Subaru Ascent and the emulator's CAN 'car' scenario.

title: HOME Menu manual for the .cia (Manual button)
description:
The 3DS HOME Menu has a Manual button that opens an electronic manual packed in an installed title (owner screenshot, 2026-11-15). Add one to gaugeboy.cia with several sections (e.g. Getting started, Wi-Fi setup, DIAG, Clearing codes, Safety). Only the .cia gets it; the .3dsx (Homebrew Launcher) has no Manual button.

How it works: the manual is optional CIA content index 1, a CFA added with makerom (e.g. -content manual.cfa:1:1). Its romfs holds Manual.bcma, an uncompressed DARC archive of LZ10-compressed DARC archives (page layouts and textures). See https://www.3dbrew.org/wiki/BCMA and https://3dbrew.org/wiki/Makerom.

No ready-made tool builds a .bcma from scratch. Build it from our own files only (the repo is public and MIT; Nintendo's manual files can't be relicensed), with a script in tools/; a new tool needs owner approval (CLAUDE.md section 9).

Plan: 1) spike a one-page manual made only from our own files and check it opens from the HOME Menu on the owner's New 3DS; 2) if it works, generate it from the same text as an in-app HELP / docs/manual.md so they stay in step; 3) add it to make cia and the release workflow.

title: Idea: use the adapter in STA mode (joined to a phone hotspot or home Wi-Fi) instead of its V-LINK network
description: Vgate says the iCar Pro's Wi-Fi module switches from AP mode (its own V-LINK network) to STA mode (joins another network) once you log in to its page at 192.168.0.10; a teardown thread reports AT commands (+++, a, AT+WMODE=STA, AT+WSSSID=...). In STA mode the adapter and the 3DS could share a network that has internet (home Wi-Fi, phone hotspot): the 3DS connection test would pass normally, no manual DNS. Unknowns/risks before trying: how to get back to AP mode (no documented reset; a stranded adapter may be unrecoverable), whether an iPhone hotspot lets two clients talk to each other, and finding the adapter's new DHCP address (GaugeBoy would need a port-35000 scan or a config.ini host). Only test with a spare adapter. Not needed: the current AP-mode setup works.
